The constrained laptop tier keeps its hardware budget plus a budget-safe creative subset.
Test Result / Notes: E1: detect_tier()->cloud_cinematic when cloud_available so generation uses the directive (was constrained on the laptop, wasting cloud headroom). Verified real runtime prompt is cinematic with no 8GB budget; tests/test_cinematic_directive.py (5). Suite 106/106.

User Story: As the system, when the Judge rejects a defect I remember the reason + offending code so the generator never makes the SAME mistake twice.
Expected Behaviour: On every Judge REPAIR/REJECT, log_judge_rejection() records each reason (line-number-agnostic signature) + a code snippet to data/judge_rejections.json, deduped with a count. On the next generation, get_judge_avoidance_modifiers() injects a 'MISTAKES THE JUDGE HAS REJECTED BEFORE - DO NOT REPEAT' block into the system prompt (ranked by frequency, bounded). /stats surfaces the learned-lessons count. 30-day TTL.
Test Result / Notes: New feature this session. tests/test_judge_rejection_memory.py (7): record, dedupe-across-line-numbers, distinct lessons, learn-after-first, noise-ignored, bounded, frequency-ranked. Wired in bot.py (judge loop + prompt + /stats). Suite 117/117.

User Story: As a viewer, I get a professionally DIRECTED explainer (planned beats, timing, camera moves, transitions, semantic color, narration) because the system storyboards the film BEFORE writing any code.
Expected Behaviour: Before code generation, generate_storyboard() produces a JSON IR: title, concept, duration_target, semantic palette, and 4-7 beats (purpose, start/end, objects, action, camera, transition_in, emphasis, narration). parse_storyboard validates structure; validate_storyboard critiques it as a composition (narrative arc, contiguous timeline vs target, semantic palette, camera-move-needs-reason, crowding) non-fatally. format_storyboard_for_codegen compiles it into an AUTHORITATIVE beat-by-beat spec injected into the codegen system prompt (supersedes the lighter scene-layout plan); per-beat narration seeds the voiceover. Gated by STORYBOARD_ENABLED (default True); any failure falls back to the scene-layout plan + prior behavior.
Test Result / Notes: Re-architecture pillar #1 (user-chosen). New module storyboard.py; llm.generate_storyboard (reasoning-on); prompt_builder storyboard injection (storyboard wins over scene_plan); bot.py wiring (storyboard-first, graceful fallback) + narration hookup; config STORYBOARD_ENABLED. tests/test_storyboard.py (14). Suite 127/127; bot imports clean. Foundation for narration-sync + best-of-N.

Trigger: Any animation request when BEST_OF_N > 1 and cloud farm is available
User Story: As a viewer, I get the BEST animation out of N diverse candidates — not just the first one the model happens to produce — because the system generates N candidates, renders them all as drafts on the cloud farm in parallel, vision-ranks the ACTUAL rendered frames, and ships the winner.
Expected Behaviour: When BEST_OF_N > 1 and cloud_available(): (1) generate N candidates concurrently, each with its own storyboard IR for diversity; (2) render all N as drafts (-ql, 15fps) in parallel on the cloud farm; (3) vision-score each draft on its actual keyframes (reusing visual_critic.critique_render); (4) return the highest-scoring candidate's code. The main pipeline then renders the winner at full quality + polishes. Fully graceful: gen failure → remaining candidates; all renders fail → first candidate unranked; all scoring fails → score=0; nothing generates → None (falls back to single-candidate). Gated by BEST_OF_N config (default 1 = disabled). n clamped to minimum 2. Invalid code (no GenScene/construct) filtered before rendering.
Test Result / Notes: Re-architecture pillar #2 (highest visible quality jump). New module best_of_n.py (118 lines); bot.py wiring (Step 2 in pipeline, gated + graceful fallback); config BEST_OF_N + BEST_OF_N_DRAFT_QUALITY; /stats surfaces tournament config. tests/test_best_of_n.py (11): picks highest score, all-gen-fail → None, all-render-fail → unranked, partial gen failure, scoring failure, n clamp, invalid code filtered. Suite 138/138; bot imports clean.

User Story: As a viewer, a rich topic gets a longer (up to ~90s), information-dense explainer that covers every key sub-point (definition, intuition, derivation, worked example, misconception, recap), while a trivial ask stays short and my 8 GB laptop renders stay modest and safe.
Expected Behaviour: recommend_depth(prompt, tier) -> compact|standard|deep (constrained tier ALWAYS compact; capable tiers: COMPLEX->deep, else standard). Depth threads into the storyboard: build_storyboard_prompt(depth) injects a DEPTH & COVERAGE block (beats 4-6/6-9/8-12, duration 25-40/40-60/60-90s, key_points 3-4/4-6/6-9). The IR gains a top-level key_points list (surfaced as a COVER EVERY POINT checklist) + 1-3 teaching sentences of narration per beat. build_complexity_modifier and CINEMATIC_STYLE request 7-12 beats and full coverage on capable tiers. Narration is sized to the video (~1.5-2 words/sec from the storyboard's duration_target_s) and preserves the detailed script. Capacity raised so longer != truncated/under-reviewed: code-gen tokens 24576->32768, Judge reviews 16000 chars (was 6000). Constrained 8 GB tier keeps compact/short and its weight-threshold/downgrade behavior.
Test Result / Notes: Plan 'Longer, more information-dense animations'. prompt_builder (recommend_depth, scaled complexity modifier, CINEMATIC_STYLE 7-12 beats + cover-fully); storyboard (_DEPTH_PROFILES, key_points field+checklist, parameterized prompt, validate upper-bound 14 + key_points note); llm.generate_storyboard(depth=, max_tokens 8192); bot (depth selection + thread to both storyboard calls, narration sizing); config MANIM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 32768; judge_ai code window 16000. Tests: depth bands/key_points (test_storyboard) + recommend_depth/scaled durations (test_prompt_complexity). Suite 160/160; bot imports clean.
